item.title: [Перевод] Дэвид Л. Парнас «Аспекты распределения информации в методологии проектирования»
item.description: В начале 1970-х программные системы уже не помещались в голове одного человека, а документация порой росла быстрее, чем код. Парнас задался вопросом, которого до него, кажется, никто не задавал: а нужно ли вообще, чтобы каждый программист знал о системе все? Его ответ — нет, и именно из этого «нет» выросло то, что мы сегодня называем инкапсуляцией. Читать далее

item.title: MintFlow: Minimal Trajectory Intervention for Constrained Flow Matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.02260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flow matching models excel at generative modeling, and many downstream applications require their samples to satisfy prescribed constraints, such as observed measurements and physical laws. item.title: Fast Models, Slow Evidence: A Paired and Self-Audited Evaluation of System-1 Decision Models for LLM Agent Harnesses
item.description: arXiv:2610.02267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent harnesses make many small, typed decisions per task: which model to call, which tool to use, whether retrieved text is relevant, whether an input carries an injection. System-1 decision models answer such questions in a single forward pass with class probabilities, promising large cost and latency savings over LLM calls. item.title: The AI Risk Observatory: What Can We Learn from AI Disclosures in Annual Reports About Societal Resilience?
item.description: arXiv:2610.02281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Societal resilience research relies on access to useful and actionable data, which motivates our main research question: Can annual reports, processed at scale with LLMs, provide a useful signal about how companies disclose their response to AI? item.title: Keep It CALM: Analyzing the Limits of Global Unsafety in Text-to-Image Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.02300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training-free safeguards for text-to-image generation often rely on a reusable safety signal, such as an unsafe direction or global toxic subspace, applied broadly across prompts. item.title: Choosing Before Acting: Comparative Value Estimation for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.02330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) rely on long-horizon tool invocation sequences for complex tasks, where each invocation can alter the task state and condition subsequent decisions. item.title: World Editing: Intervening on Executable Worlds at Increasing Depth
item.description: arXiv:2610.02331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive world models are increasingly capable of generating environments and acting within them, yet deliberately editing an existing executable world remains underexplored. item.title: DeReAct: Decomposed Reasoning and Acting for Reliable AI Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.02351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ReAct-based agents typically rely on a single LLM policy to propose actions, interact with the environment, and decide when a task is complete. item.title: Traversing the Satisfaction-Diversity Frontier in Text-to-Image Diffusion
